question: Which edition of the World Sustainable Development Summit (WSDS) was held from 5th to 7th March 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**24th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 24th edition of the World Sustainable Development Summit (WSDS) was held from **5th to 7th March 2025**.
 
• WSDS is the annual flagship event of **The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI)**.
 
• This summit brings together global leaders, policymakers, researchers, and corporates to discuss and deliberate on **issues related to sustainable development and climate change.**
 
• The 2025 summit focused on **“Driving Green Transitions: Advancing Inclusive and Sustainable Growth”** as its theme.
 
• It emphasized the need for collective global actions to address environmental challenges while ensuring equitable growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Sustainable Development Summit (WSDS):**

 
 
• WSDS was launched in 2001 as the Delhi Sustainable Development Summit (DSDS).
 
• It is a platform to foster partnerships for sustainable development and environmental conservation.
 
• The summit addresses critical topics like climate change, energy transitions, water security, and green financing.
 
• Prominent global stakeholders, including heads of states, Nobel laureates, and leading scientists, participate annually.
 
 
 
• **The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI):**
 
 
• TERI is a non-profit research institution based in New Delhi, India, established in 1974.
 
• It specializes in **energy, environment, and sustainable development research.**
 
• TERI is committed to promoting environmentally sound and equitable development globally.
 
 
 
• **Green Transitions:**
 
 
• Green transitions refer to the shift towards low-carbon, resource-efficient, and socially inclusive economies.
 
• This involves adopting renewable energy, sustainable practices, and technologies to mitigate climate change effects.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change:**
 
 
• Climate change refers to long-term shifts in temperatures and weather patterns, primarily caused by human activities like burning fossil fuels.
 
• Global efforts like the **Paris Agreement** aim to limit global temperature rise to below 2°C compared to pre-industrial levels.
